# SPD-007 — Ledger CLI v1: bin/spud (init, migrate, import, render, ticket and member commands)

## Brief
Build the one program that writes the ledger, as specified in [[SPD-006]]'s spike (`docs/spikes/2026-09-12-ledger-database.md`: Recommendation, Proposed schema, Concurrency model, Migration plan, Language recommendation). Python 3.14 stdlib only, one file `bin/spud`, invoked `python3.14 -I -S`. Scope from the spike's proposal 1: `init`, `migrate`, `backup`, `config sync`, `import`, `render`, `ticket new|move|edit|show`, `member new|log|result|block|finish`, `proposal file|decide`, `handoff add`, `report add`, `board`, `fleet`, `card`, `doctor`, `settings sync`, all with `--json`. `settings sync` also generates the two env caps in `.claude/settings.json` from `spud.config.json` (the spike's proposal 9, folded in here). WAL, `busy_timeout = 5000`, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on every write, column ownership checked on `--as`, limits as `count(*)` inside the insert transaction, timestamps from the clock.

Acceptance test before any cutover: import the markdown-v0 ledger into a scratch database, render it to a scratch directory, diff against the committed files until only formatting differs. Cutover (real `spud init`, `import`, `render`, one commit) is the last step and is Eric's go.

Decided by Eric, 2026-09-12: the database is `.spud/ledger.db` in this repo, gitignored (question 1); **per-project ticket prefixes** (question 2, against the spike's recommendation), so `tickets.key` is `<prefix>-<n>` with a counter per project, the prefixes live on the `projects` row (`spud.config.json`'s `tickets.prefix` and `teams.prefix` become the home project's values), and the team key follows the same rule; fan-out limits count children **alive at once** (`status IN ('planned','active')` under the parent), not children ever planned, while IDs keep counting every child ever planned (question 3); generated notes are read-only, with the hash check and `spud import --file` as designed (question 4); reports render from events and `spud report add` takes only the Next line (question 7); `synchronous = NORMAL` (question 9).

Done when: `bin/spud` passes the scratch acceptance test; `spud doctor` reports the interpreter and SQLite version; the DDL matches the spike's or every difference is written down in the ticket; nothing cut over yet.

## Size, persona and model decision
Large: an engineer lead with a team. **Tier override: fable instead of opus.** Reason: data and persistence, expensive if wrong, as the spike's proposal says and the persona table allows. A reviewer on fable checks the import-render diff before the lead returns.

## Outcome
Shipped `bin/spud` (2,895 lines, Python 3.14 stdlib only, `#!/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14`, run as `python3.14 -I -S bin/spud …`) and `tests/` (12 files, 124 stdlib unittest tests) by [[SPUD-007/Atlantic|Atlantic]] (01, engineer, fable), reviewed twice by [[SPUD-007/Annabelle|Annabelle]] (01.01, reviewer, fable). Commands: `init`, `migrate`, `backup`, `config sync`, `settings sync --path --dry-run`, `import [DIRS] | --file PATH`, `render [--out DIR] [--discard PATH]`, `ticket new|move|edit|show`, `member new|start|log|result|block|finish|edit|show`, `proposal file|decide|list`, `handoff add`, `report add`, `board [--brief]`, `fleet`, `card`, `events`, `doctor`; all take `--json` and `--as spud | SPUD-nnn/<Name> | SPUD-nnn/<lineage> | <agent_id>`; exit codes 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 ownership, 4 limit, 5 transition, 6 render conflict. WAL, `busy_timeout 5000`, `synchronous NORMAL`, `foreign_keys ON`, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on every write (traced by Annabelle), limits as `count(*)` inside the insert transaction, clock timestamps.

Verified: Spud's own run at HEAD 2f11506, `Ran 124 tests in 27.983s` / `OK`; the acceptance round trip (import the committed markdown-v0 ledger into a temp database, render to a temp directory, diff) is formatting-only, in two forms: a corpus pinned at commit 2f11506 with the exact 32 (file, section) pairs kept as verbatim prose, and a live-HEAD cutover-readiness check with no fixed count. `spud doctor` prints python 3.14.7 and SQLite 3.53.4. Annabelle's attacks: ownership refusals (every wrong actor, exit 3 or 1), limits (exit 4, exact under 6 and 12 concurrent plans), the lead race (01 in 12 of 12 after the fix), the render conflict end to end, both state machines, 120 concurrent writers with zero lock errors. No `.spud/` in the repo; nothing cut over.

DDL differences from the spike's Proposed schema, each intended: (1) per-project prefixes (Eric's decision 2): `projects.ticket_prefix` and `projects.team_prefix` (UNIQUE), `tickets.number` with `UNIQUE (project_id, number)`, `tickets.id` a plain surrogate, keys computed as `<prefix>-%03d` from `max(number) + 1` per project inside the insert transaction; (2) fan-out counts children alive (`status IN ('planned','active')`) under the parent (decision 3), a query change only, lineage still counts every child ever planned; (3) `tickets.heading`: three committed tickets shorten the H1 against `title`; (4) `tickets.layout` and `members.layout`: the committed files vary in frontmatter key presence, key order and section order, and the render reproduces each file's layout; (5) table `imported_sections`: markdown-v0 prose the rows cannot regenerate, kept verbatim with a per-section watermark (32 sections in the pinned corpus), because the spike says known dirt is imported, not cleaned; (6) `renders.content`: the text last written, so `import --file` is a three-way accept; (7) two event kinds added to the CHECK, `member.edited` and `config.synced`. Also a render rule, not DDL: the generated-file marker sits immediately after the frontmatter, never before it, because Obsidian reads properties only from a block at byte 0.

Decisions by Spud during the run (Eric may overrule any): `import --file` is Spud-only and, reading decision 4 narrowly, accepts only a ticket's title, priority, tags, status (through the state machine), Brief, Size and Outcome, a member's Brief, Outcome and status, and an appended report entry, refusing everything derived, timestamped or member-owned with the command that changes it; `blocked → active` exists as the re-brief path (`member start`), a re-spawn being a new row; `member new` requires a non-empty brief; `member start` is the parent's until SPD-008's hooks take the transition; any ancestor may record a member (Law 9 when a lead dies); imported rows invent no timestamp (`closed_at` NULL, derived NOT NULL columns named in the import event).

Left: the code lives on branch `spd-007-ledger-cli`; merging it is Eric's call, and cutover (`spud init`, `import`, `render`, one commit) is a separate go. For [[SPD-008]] or later: nothing stops a finished member from logging, a parent from finishing over live children, or a ticket from closing with live members; `render`, `config sync` and `backup` take no actor; `--version` and usage errors are not JSON. [[SPD-009]] rewrites the protocol around these commands. `.gitignore` for `.spud/` and `__pycache__/` is [[SPD-012]].
